name: Diabetic Hospital Diet (Consistent Carbohydrate)
description: Consistent-carbohydrate meal pattern with limits on added sugar, saturated fat and sodium, and a fiber target.
disclaimer: Thresholds are illustrative and codified from public guidance. Individual carbohydrate targets should be set by a clinical dietitian; verify against your institution's approved diet manual before clinical use.

rules.title: Carbohydrate per main meal

evidence.source: ADA Standards of Care: Nutrition therapy; consistent-carbohydrate meal planning
evidence.note: 45-60 g carbohydrate per meal is a widely used starting range for adults; individualize with a dietitian.

rules.remedy: Adjust starch, fruit or dairy portions to bring the meal into the 45-60 g range.

rules.title: Carbohydrate per snack

evidence.source: ADA Standards of Care: Nutrition therapy; consistent-carbohydrate meal planning
evidence.note: Snacks commonly contain 15-30 g carbohydrate in consistent-carbohydrate plans.

rules.remedy: Size the snack to 15-30 g carbohydrate, pairing with protein or fat if needed.

rules.title: Added sugar share of energy

evidence.source: WHO Guideline: Sugars intake for adults and children (2015); US Dietary Guidelines for Americans
evidence.note: Free/added sugars should be less than 10% of total energy intake.

rules.remedy: Remove sweetened beverages, desserts and sweetened condiments.

rules.title: Saturated fat share of energy

evidence.source: ADA Standards of Care; US Dietary Guidelines for Americans
evidence.note: Limit saturated fat to less than 10% of daily calories.

rules.remedy: Swap fatty meats and full-fat dairy for lean protein and unsaturated fats.

rules.title: Fiber density

evidence.note: Aim for about 14 g fiber per 1,000 kcal.

rules.remedy: Add whole grains, legumes, vegetables or fruit.

rules.title: Daily sodium limit

evidence.source: ADA Standards of Care; US Dietary Guidelines for Americans
evidence.note: Limit sodium to less than 2,300 mg per day.

rules.remedy: Replace processed foods with fresh alternatives.

rules.title: Prohibited high-sugar items

evidence.source: ADA Standards of Care: Nutrition therapy
evidence.note: Sugar-sweetened beverages and concentrated sweets should be minimized or avoided.

rules.remedy: Substitute water, unsweetened beverages or sugar-free alternatives.

rules.title: Minimum meal frequency

evidence.note: Regular, evenly spaced eating occasions support consistent glycemic control.

rules.remedy: Add a meal or snack so the day has at least three eating occasions.

rules.title: Day-to-day carbohydrate consistency

evidence.note: Consistent-carbohydrate plans keep total daily carbohydrate similar from day to day.

rules.remedy: Rebalance carbohydrate so the highest and lowest days differ by no more than 45 g.
